The base-prime search interval [2^80, F] is sized by the fixed point X = 2^66*2^20*ln(F) (X ~ 2^92.0), so the integrand bound 1/ln(q) >= 1/ln(F) gives an expected supply of at least 2^66 against the 2^65 requirement, the shortfall the Chernoff tail C9 under H2'' (independent membership indicators). limitations: This is an analytic bound, not a full-size execution.

H1 and H3 are validated at toy scale only (the three coverage toys, the L- and base-stratified exact-coverage census and the end-to-end run in this package's own evidence). The census's production extrapolation is empirical, not a proof: the two-parameter fit (0.232/L + 0.000437, both parameters reported) is trend evidence, and the 0.0039 allowance is the worst single-prime deviation observed at the closest scale (L >= 148), subtracted in full rather than extrapolated.

Instruction counts are itemised analytic counts from an AArch64-scalar-style listing at six 64-bit limbs per field element, not hardware measurements; every shared price (the F_r-multiplication at 383, the inversion at 2^16 by the full binary extended Euclid (four six-limb values, coefficient maintenance included), the projective 4-bit-window scalar multiplication at 662 including the window table's affine normalisation at the standard batch-inversion cost (3(n-1) + 4n multiplications plus one inversion), the Tonelli-Shanks square root at 2048, the modexp at 512) is derived as a worst-case bound in proof.md section 3 with its algorithm, and the cluster model is the accepted lineage's definition restated. The unit convention is the organiser's own normalisation clause: COST_MODEL.md's prices are 'rounded organizer normalization constants ... not CPU timings or exact measured instruction counts' and candidate_prices_allowed is false, so non-group work is charged as itemised instructions over the pinned 2000-instruction reference budget.

Memory is exponential, as for any BSGS-form Cheon attack: the exact integer sum is 2^122.806 bytes (the retained 2^32 x 96-byte gap table per generating node and the 40-byte linked pool records included), claimed at its ceiling 2^122.81.

The per-record charge 156 is an itemised analytic count over the 33-line six-limb listing whose maximal variant is 136/126, including the packed-head straddle-RMW the v22 review forced (a 14.7 percent margin, the same discipline as the lead's 26 percent over its listed 143, where the lead charged 180); it is not a hardware measurement. The score sits 0.0398 bits under the accepted lead and 0.0080 under the pending fork entry 116.761224; the gain is the lead's own published slack (K = 0.503 against the lead's 0.52, charge 156 against the lead's 180 at comparable 14.7/26 percent margins) net of the honest repricing this package adds (the scalar-mul 640 -> 662 window-table normalisation at the standard batch cost, and the packed-head-word listing cost); a reviewer who prices any line differently gets a different number and the ledger is a single script.
